title: Causal Masks vs Bidirectional Attention
interviewAnswer: Causal masks prevent tokens from attending to future positions for autoregressive next-token prediction; bidirectional encoders can attend to both sides under different objectives.
why: Masking determines what information a token is allowed to use.
intuition: A next-token model cannot peek at the answer to its right.
deepDive: Causal attention sets future logits to -∞ before softmax; padding masks solve a different batching problem.
commonMistakes: Training autoregressive objectives with future leakage.
followUps: How does masking interact with KV cache?
production: Mask bugs can silently leak labels or break variable-length serving.
workedExample: When predicting “sat” in “the cat sat”, the model can attend to “the cat” but not future tokens.
